note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 41) on data/benches/vacuum.json: pressure. Boiled, the flask's steam drives its air out; stoppered and cooled, the steam condenses and leaves a partial vacuum, where water boils far below 100 C; heated hard, the steam's pressure pops the stopper. Its waits are timed from data/sessions/pressure.json (Stage 28).
title: Experiment: boiling under a vacuum

steps.title: A burner under the flask
steps.text: Pick up the burner in Supplies on the left, then click the flask: it goes under it.
steps.why: The flask holds 100 g of water and, above it, about 150 mL of air.

checks.text: the burner is under the flask

steps.title: Light it
steps.text: Right-click the burner to choose it, then drag its valve, in the column on the right, all the way open.

checks.text: time runs at least 60 times faster

steps.title: Boil the air out
steps.text: Wait for the water to boil. Point at the flask: the readout shows the gas over the water.
steps.why: Boiling water makes steam faster than the mouth lets it go: the steam pushes the air out of the flask, until there is only steam over the water.

checks.text: less than 2 mg of nitrogen left in the flask

steps.title: Off the heat
steps.text: Choose the burner and shut its valve.

steps.title: Stopper it at once
steps.text: Pick up the stopper in Supplies, then click the flask.
steps.why: The flask is full of steam and nothing else. Wait, and as it cools it would draw the room's air back in.

checks.text: the stopper is in the flask

steps.title: A monitor
steps.text: Drag a monitor out of the parts drawer, beside the outbox, onto a free square of the bench.
steps.why: A monitor reads a quantity for you, all the time.

steps.title: Let it sense the flask
steps.text: Drag from the monitor's sensing port, the dot at its foot, onto the flask. Its settings open.

steps.title: Its pressure
steps.why: Sealed, the flask has its own pressure: what its gas pushes on the walls with. Open, it is always the room's, 101.3 kPa.

steps.title: Below 10 kPa
steps.text: Click "below". Then click the value, type 10, and click "set".
steps.why: Its lamp lights once the flask's pressure falls below a tenth of the room's.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: Wait, and watch the monitor and the readout's pressure fall.
steps.why: As the flask cools, its steam condenses back into water. With no air behind it, what is left is a near vacuum: the pressure of water's own vapour, a few kPa at room temperature.

steps.title: A gentle flame
steps.text: Choose the burner and set its valve to about a fifth open.

steps.title: It boils at 50 C
steps.text: Wait for the water to reach 50 C, and read the flask's pressure.
steps.why: Water boils where its vapour pushes as hard as what is over it. Under 101.3 kPa that takes 100 C; under 12 kPa, 50 C. Every bit of heat now turns more water to steam, and the pressure climbs with the temperature.

steps.title: The full flame
steps.text: Open the burner's valve all the way.

steps.title: Until the stopper pops
steps.text: Wait. The notices, at the top, say what happens.
steps.why: Past 100 C the steam's pressure is more than the room's: it pushes on the stopper until its grip gives way.

checks.text: the stopper is out of the flask

steps.title: Off
steps.text: Choose the burner and shut its valve.

fails.text: The stopper went in with air still in the flask: cooled, the air keeps the pressure up, and there is no vacuum. Press reset to start again.
The flask burst. Press reset to start again.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged
